messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime p95/p99 regression detected for service `inference-stream-v2` in prod-us-east-1. p95=420ms (SLO=200ms), p99=2.1s (SLO=1s). Metric spike began ~14:06Z. Alert ID INC-20260314-01.

alice_oncall: I'm on it — paging SREs and platform. Starting initial checks. @ben_c can you pull the streaming dashboard and trace sample logs?

ben_c: looking now. Dashboard shows sustained increase in stream tail latency around 14:05Z. Concurrent streaming sessions up ~30%. No mass error spike (5xx stays low). CPU on inference nodes ~65-75%, GPU mem usage normal. Queue depth (stream-inflight) up on the frontend router.

carol_sre: possible backlog at the grpc frontend or per-connection KV cache thrash. Can we get a tail of the streaming router logs?

ben_c: pasted relevant excerpt:
```
2026-03-14T14:06:08Z router-1 pool=us-east-1-shard-3 inflight=342 backlog=124 accept_ms=12 dispatch_ms=3 token_ms=8
2026-03-14T14:06:11Z router-2 pool=us-east-1-shard-3 inflight=410 backlog=190 accept_ms=22 dispatch_ms=18 token_ms=110
2026-03-14T14:06:14Z router-2 pool=us-east-1-shard-3 inflight=425 backlog=215 accept_ms=35 dispatch_ms=45 token_ms=160
```
Looks like token_ms jumps correlate with p99.

doug_prod: any recent rollout? I saw a non-critical canary earlier today but it was a config tweak for batching.

observability-bot: Canary deploy `inference-v2-batch-0.9` promoted at 2026-03-14T12:03Z (metadata: batching=aggressive, kv_cache=enabled). No immediate errors flagged during canary.

alice_oncall: quick checks: 1) Are we hitting a single shard hot spot? 2) Is streaming path degraded while non-streaming gen is fine? 3) Are autoscalers healthy?

ben_c: Non-streaming gen p95 mostly within SLO; streaming is the outlier. Heatmap shows traffic skewed to shard-3 (~40% of streams). Autoscaler for shard-3 reporting throttle events (scale cooldowns).

carol_sre: mitigation options — a) shift traffic off shard-3 via routing policy to even distribution, b) bump shard-3 desired count to add capacity, c) enable fallback to non-streaming short-poll for affected customers. Suggest we try routing first (least disruptive).

alice_oncall: Agreed. Do routing change first. @doug_prod can you trigger route override for 15m to even distribution? Include a gradual drain.

doug_prod: running command now:
```
# route override - distribute streams evenly across us-east-1 shards
redwoodctl route set --service inference-stream-v2 --region us-east-1 --policy even --duration 15m --reason "p99 spike triage"
```
Applying... done. Observing metrics in 90s.

ben_c: after route change p95 down to ~260ms after ~2m, p99 still elevated at ~1.3s but trending down. Inflight counts redistributed; shard-3 inflight back to ~210.

alice_oncall: good. keep monitoring. We'll also prepare to scale if p99 doesn't return to baseline. @sre-runbook-bot show runbook for stream latency degradation.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook: Stream tail latency > SLO steps — 1) check shard distribution, 2) route override, 3) scale shard, 4) enable non-stream fallback, 5) notify customers. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/stream-tail-latency

carol_sre: flag — token_ms in logs suggests occasional long token generation on some nodes (160ms). Could be model kv-cache eviction thrash or a kernel fallback. I'm opening a short profiling trace against a warm node.

ben_c: profiling attached (summary): small fraction of requests hit `kv_cache_miss` + `kernel_fallback` path. Misses spiked after canary tweak to batching; batching may increase working set and evict hot keys.

alice_oncall: action items now: 1) Dougs routing override (done) 2) Carol to trace and push KV cache adjustments 3) Ben to watch SLIs and prepare scale command 4) I'll notify customers with status update.

doug_prod: if p99 doesn't fall below 1s in next 10m I'll scale shard-3 by +2 replicas. Let me know to proceed.

carol_sre: applying conservative KV cache config rollback to prior policy (reduce aggressive eviction). Command:
```
redwoodctl config update --service inference-stream-v2 --kv-cache.eviction_policy=LRU --kv-cache.size=12GB --reason="rollback canary eviction"
```
Rollback applied.

observability-bot: after config rollback and routing change: p95=220ms, p99=980ms, error rate unchanged.

ben_c: p99 just crossed below 1s — currently 940ms and trending stable. Looks like combined routing+rollback did it.

alice_oncall: excellent. I'll post preliminary incident update to #general and to the ticket. Preliminary impact: increased tail latency for streams in us-east-1 from 14:05Z to 14:28Z. Estimated affected customers: ~12 customers experienced degraded streaming latency; 3 customers with heavy sessions saw noticeable degradation but no failures. No data loss.

doug_prod: scaling not required. Will keep monitoring for 30m then revert route override at 14:40Z.

carol_sre: follow-up: we'll schedule a deeper postmortem to investigate why batching change affected kv-cache working set. Also propose a canary gate for eviction policy changes.

alice_oncall: handoff: I'm taking notes and will hand to @ben_c at 14:45Z for 2hr follow-up. If anything regresses, page SRE immediately.

ben_c: acknowledged — I'll run a 2hr watch and start an artifacts collection (heap profiles, kernel fallback traces, routing logs).

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-20260314-01 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Started: 2026-03-14T14:06Z Mitigated: 2026-03-14T14:28Z Impact: degraded stream tail latency in prod-us-east-1.

alice_oncall: closing thread for now — will open postmortem doc and link here once created. :thumbsup:
